integrity: The argument uses unitary Fourier decomposition, dual annihilator counting, exact finite combinatorial enumeration and monotone cosine gap comparison; code checks are finite consistency tests. No independent audit or certification was performed.
scientific_limitations: The first formula assumes an odd-order finite abelian normal subgroup, precisely two distinct unweighted taps in each coset and the complex left-regular Hilbert space. The three-way census and sharp spectral-gap result require elementary abelian odd-prime A, d>=2, and the gap assumes independent differences. No weighted, even-order, other-coset-split, or dependent-gap classification is asserted. General Fourier block decomposition is classical; a broader historical implication remains possible. Finite checker experiments corroborate rather than replace the proof.
title: Balanced four-tap generalized-dihedral convolution: three nullity strata and a sharp quadratic spectral gap
